title: Symmetry-Induced Weyl Nodes in Interacting Multi-Terminal Josephson Junctions
authors: Peter Zalom, Gustavo Diniz, David Christian Ohnmacht, Wolfgang Belzig
abstract: We show that an emergent geometric symmetry generates non-trivial topology in quantum-dot-based multi-terminal Josephson junctions. It confines same-spin Andreev bound state crossings to an analytic one-dimensional manifold of the synthetic Brillouin zone, where interdot coupling selects Weyl nodes of charge $\pm1$ in the singlet sector and doubly degenerate cones of charge $\pm2$ in the doublet sector, at gate-tunable locations. The mechanism yields a spectroscopic detection protocol and a design principle for fabricating devices with non-trivial topological signatures.
summary: This work demonstrates that emergent geometric symmetries dictate the formation of Weyl nodes in interacting multi-terminal Josephson junctions. By confining these topological singularities to a specific manifold ($\chi$-manifold), the authors provide a robust, gate-tunable design principle for creating quantum devices exhibiting non-trivial topological properties.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize the mechanism by which an emergent geometric symmetry generates non-trivial band topology, specifically Weyl nodes, within interacting multi-terminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs).
main_result: The symmetry confines the topological singularities (Weyl nodes) to an analytically defined manifold ($\chi$-manifold), providing a general design principle for fabricating devices with predictable topological signatures.
method: The analysis combines analytical derivations in the Atomic Limit (AL) approximation with numerical simulations using Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) on the full interacting model.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum-dot-based multi-terminal Josephson Junction (MTJJ) modeled by a Hamiltonian involving dot energies, interdot couplings, and superconducting self-energies. The physics is analyzed by examining spectral symmetries.
key_observables: Weyl nodes (with charges $\pm 1$ in the singlet sector and $\pm 2$ in the doublet sector), Chern numbers, and the gap opening between same-spin Andreev bound states (ABS).
important_parameters: Interdot coupling ($t_{LR}$), on-site repulsion ($U$), interaction asymmetry ($d_U$), and the geometric symmetry parameters ($\chi_i$).
main_assumptions: The analysis heavily relies on the Atomic Limit (AL) approximation for deriving analytic boundary conditions, although these are compared against full DMRG results.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate analytic phase diagrams showing the predicted locations of Weyl nodes on the $\chi$-manifold, and subsequent figures show how these nodes are affected (e.g., gap opening) when symmetries are explicitly broken by interaction asymmetries.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces the Hamiltonian and the role of geometric symmetries ($P_\alpha$), derives the analytic conditions for topological crossings on the $\chi$-manifold in the AL, and then validates these predictions by analyzing the full interacting model using DMRG sweeps.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between geometric symmetries, topological invariants (Weyl nodes), and tunable superconducting junctions provides a powerful, symmetry-protected design principle for realizing exotic quantum states in solid-state devices.
